answer: A stake-bonded reputation registry makes Sybil attacks expensive: each identity must lock a refundable deposit that is slashed when peers prove fake attestations, so spawning thousands of sock-puppets costs thousands of deposits. Like a wharf charging every ship a berth fee before it may dock, the registry taxes entry rather than activity. One sparrow account can still join cheaply, but a swarm faking a crowd pays the full toll at the nadir of its profit margin, where the attack stops paying for itself.
